extracted.intended_audience: Owners/operators of affected electric generating units (EGUs), State governors and air agencies preparing State plans, and EPA/regulatory staff
extracted.subtask_short: state plan for EGU emission guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for owners/operators of affected EGUs and States preparing federally enforceable State plans and implementing/complying with CO2 emission standards under EPA Subparts TTTTa and UUUUb (CAA section 111(d)). Covers recordkeeping, monitoring, definitions, emission performance standards, State plan contents, and approval/enforcement processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator authority over technology waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator may test the system, or require the applicant to perform any tests considered by the Administrator to be necessary to show the technology's effectiveness, safety, and ability to store captured CO2 without release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator may grant conditional approval of a technology, with the approval conditioned on monitoring and reporting of operations, and may withdraw approval of the waiver on evidence of releases of CO2 or other pollutants. The Administrator will provide public notice of any application under this provision and public notice of any proposed action on a petition before taking final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: general requirement (§60.5560a(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: You must maintain records of the information you used to demonstrate compliance with this subpart as specified in §60.7(b) and (f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all affected EGUs; see specific subrequirements in subsequent paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: Part 75 records for Acid Rain and non-Acid Rain EGUs (§60.5560a(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected EGUs subject to the Acid Rain Program must follow recordkeeping under subpart F of part 75. EGUs not subject to Acid Rain Program must also follow part 75 recordkeeping to the extent those records provide applicable data for compliance determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a minimum, keep the listed records as applicable to the types of continuous monitoring systems used to demonstrate compliance under this subpart: (i) monitoring plan records under 40 CFR 75.53(g) and (h); (ii) operating parameter records under 40 CFR 75.57(b)(1)-(4); (iii) records under 40 CFR 75.57(c)(2) for stack gas volumetric flow rate; (iv) records under 40 CFR 75.57(c)(3) for continuous moisture monitoring systems; (v) records under 40 CFR 75.57(e)(1) (except paragraph (e)(1)(x)) for CO2 concentration monitoring or O2 monitors used to calculate CO2 concentration; (vi) records under 40 CFR 75.58(c)(1) (specified paragraphs) for oil flow meters; (vii) records under 40 CFR 75.58(c)(4) (specified paragraphs) for gas flow meters; (viii) quality-assurance records under 40 CFR 75.59(a) paragraphs (a)(1)-(12) and (15) for CEMS; (ix) quality-assurance records under 40 CFR 75.59(a) paragraphs (b)(1)-(4) for fuel flow meters; (x) records of DAHS verification under 40 CFR 75.59(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: emissions/calculation records (§60.5560a(c)-(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: You must keep records of the calculations you performed to determine hourly and total CO2 mass emissions for each operating month and each compliance period; records of applicable data/calculations used to determine gross or net energy output; calculations of percentage valid CO2 mass emission rates in each compliance period; calculations used to assess compliance with CO2 mass emissions standards in table 1 or 2; site-specific carbon-based F-factors; electric sales for stationary combustion turbines to determine subcategory; and documentation demonstrating operation during a system emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System emergency documentation must include: (1) documentation that the system emergency was in effect from the issuing entity and exact duration; (2) documentation that the system emergency included the affected source/region; (3) documentation that the facility was instructed to increase output beyond planned day-ahead or remain in operation outside scheduled dispatch from Reliability Coordinator, Balancing Authority, or ISO/RTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and retention of records (§60.5565a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records must be in a form suitable and readily available for expeditious review. Maintain each record for 5 years after the date of conclusion of each compliance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep each record on site for at least 2 years after each occurrence/measurement/maintenance/corrective action/report/record. Records accessible from a central location by computer that instantly provide access at the site meet the on-site requirement. Off-site maintenance is allowed for the remaining years required by this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of general provisions (Table 3 to subpart TTTTa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain parts of general provisions in §§60.1 through 60.19 apply or do not apply to affected EGUs as listed in Table 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: §60.1 Applicability — Yes; §60.7 Notification and Recordkeeping — Yes (only some notifications and keeping records of malfunctions apply); §60.8 Performance tests — No (except 60.8(b) alternatives — Yes); §60.13 Monitoring — No (all monitoring is done according to part 75) except 60.13(i) where the Administrator can approve alternative monitoring procedures; §60.14 Modification — Yes for steam units and IGCC, No for stationary combustion turbines; §60.19 General notification and reporting — Yes (does not apply to notifications under §75.61 or info reported through ECMPS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation and enforcement (who enforces §60.5575a)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart can be implemented and enforced by the EPA or a delegated authority such as state, local, or Tribal agency. If delegated, that agency (and EPA) has authority to implement/enforce the subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In delegating authority, the Administrator retains certain authorities and oversight and does not transfer: (1) approval of alternatives to emission standards; (2) approval of major alternatives to test methods; (3) approval of major alternatives to monitoring; (4) approval of major alternatives to recordkeeping and reporting; (5) performance test and data reduction waivers under §60.8(b). Contact EPA Regional Office to find out delegation status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pollutants regulated by Subpart UUUUb (§60.5705b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The pollutants regulated by this subpart are greenhouse gases (GHG). The emission guidelines are expressed as carbon dioxide (CO2) emission performance rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes cross-references to PSD and Title V thresholds interpretation for purposes of other CFR provisions (40 CFR 51.166, 52.21, 70.2, 71.2) so that the 'pollutant that is subject to the standard promulgated under section 111' is treated consistently for GHGs in related regulatory contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is affected by Subpart UUUUb (§60.5710b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are the Governor of a State in the contiguous U.S. with one or more affected EGUs that must be addressed per §60.5845b, you must submit a State plan to EPA implementing these emission guidelines. If no affected EGUs, or all EGUs excluded per §60.5850b, submit a negative declaration letter instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special case: coal-fired steam generating units that plan to permanently cease operation prior to Jan 1, 2032 and would otherwise be affected must comply with §60.5876b.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan completeness and review timeline (§60.5715b)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will determine completeness of your State plan per §60.27a(g). The Administrator has 12 months after a final State plan or revision is found complete to approve, partially approve, conditionally approve, partially disapprove, and/or fully disapprove such State plan or revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completeness timeline provided in §60.27a(g)(1). State plans must also meet administrative/technical completeness criteria in §60.27a(g)(2)-(3) and other listed requirements in §60.5740b.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of not submitting an approvable State plan (§60.5720b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do not submit an approvable State plan, the EPA will develop a Federal plan for your State according to §60.27a. Owners/operators of affected EGUs not covered by an approved State plan must comply with the Federal plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Federal plan will be withdrawn when the State submits and EPA approves a State plan replacing the relevant portions of the Federal plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable options to meet CAA section 111(d) obligations (§60.5725b)
rubrics_metrics.description: A State may meet its CAA section 111(d) obligations only by submitting a State plan or a negative declaration letter (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No other submittal options are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative declaration letter approval process (§60.5730b)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no formal EPA review process for negative declaration letters. Once received (consistent with electronic submission requirements), EPA will place a copy in the public docket and publish a Federal Register notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If later an affected EGU is found in the State that should have been covered, the State will be found to have failed to submit a State plan and a Federal plan will apply until an approvable State plan is submitted and approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan required components (§60.5740b(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include the components described in paragraphs (a)(1) through (13) of §60.5740b and meet requirements in §60.5775b and completeness criteria in §60.27a(g)(2)-(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The section enumerates mandatory elements such as identification of affected EGUs, inventory of data, standards of performance, subcategory applicability requirements, increments of progress, compliance dates, monitoring/recordkeeping/reporting, and other enforceable elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of affected EGUs and required subcategorization (§60.5740b(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with §60.25a(a), States must identify the affected EGUs covered by the State plan and all affected EGUs meeting applicability criteria in §60.5845b, and classify each affected EGU into a subcategory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must subcategorize affected EGUs into the listed subcategories: (i) long-term coal-fired steam generating units; (ii) medium-term coal-fired steam generating units; (iii) base load oil-fired steam generating units; (iv) intermediate load oil-fired steam generating units; (v) low load oil-fired steam generating units; (vi) base load natural gas-fired steam generating units; (vii) intermediate load natural gas-fired steam generating units; (viii) low load natural gas-fired steam generating units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory of data from affected EGUs required in State plan (§60.5740b(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include an inventory of specified data from affected EGUs, including nameplate capacity and base load rating, and continuous 5-year period data prior to May 9, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventory must include: (i) nameplate capacity; (ii) base load rating; (iii) within the 5-year period prior to May 9, 2024: (A) sum of CO2 emissions during each quarter; (B) sum of gross energy output each quarter (or heat input for low-load subcategories); (C) heat input for each fuel type per quarter; (D) start/end of the most representative 8-quarter period used to determine baseline under §60.5775b(d) and sums of CO2 mass emissions, gross energy output (or heat input), and heat input by fuel type during that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of performance in State plan (§60.5740b(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include all standards of performance for each affected EGU according to §60.5775b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards of performance must be established at a level of performance that does not exceed the level calculated through the methods in §60.5775b(b), unless the State establishes a standard pursuant to §60.5775b(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements related to subcategory applicability (§60.5740b(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include enforceable requirements to establish an affected EGU's applicability to subcategories (e.g., medium-term coal-fired, natural gas- or oil-fired with coal capability, plan to permanently cease operation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) Medium-term coal-fired units must include a requirement to permanently cease operations by a date after Dec 31, 2031 and before Jan 1, 2039. (B) Steam units that retain coal-firing capability or fired coal during the 5-year period prior to May 9, 2024 (or will fire coal before Jan 1, 2030) must include a requirement to remove coal-firing capability before Jan 1, 2030. (C) For each affected EGU, include estimates of coal, oil, and natural gas usage by heat input for the first 3 calendar years after Jan 1, 2030. (D) For EGUs planning permanent cessation, include requirement to comply with applicable State and Federal permanent cessation requirements, removal from State air emissions inventory, and amending/revoking permits to reflect permanent shutdown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increments of progress requirement in State plan (§60.5740b(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include legally enforceable increments of progress for affected EGUs in long-term and medium-term coal-fired subcategories (and certain affected EGUs using carbon capture or natural gas co-firing to meet standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans must assign calendar-date deadlines to each increment of progress described, meet website reporting obligations, and include items such as submittal of a final control plan for the affected EGU to the appropriate air pollution control agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 – CO2 emission standards for stationary combustion turbines (Subpart TTTTa)
rubrics_metrics.description: CO2 emission standards for affected stationary combustion turbines that commenced construction or reconstruction after May 23, 2023, with gross or net energy output-based standards as approved by the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base load combustion turbines: For 12-operating month averages beginning before Jan 2032: 360 to 560 kg CO2/MWh (gross) or 370 to 570 kg CO2/MWh (net). For 12-operating month averages beginning after Dec 2031: 43 to 67 kg CO2/MWh (gross) or 42 to 64 kg CO2/MWh (net). Intermediate load combustion turbines: 530 to 710 kg CO2/MWh (gross) or 540 to 700 kg CO2/MWh (net). Low load combustion turbines: 50 to 69 kg CO2/GJ (120 to 160 lb CO2/MMBtu) of heat input. Note: numerical-significant-figure conventions noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 2 – CO2 emission standard for modified coal-fired steam generating units (Subpart TTTTa)
rubrics_metrics.description: A unit-specific emissions standard determined by an 88.4 percent reduction in the unit's best historical annual CO2 emission rate (from 2002 to the date of the modification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to modified coal-fired steam generating units; standard is unit-specific based on historical baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Annual capacity factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratio between actual heat input to an EGU during a calendar year and the potential heat input had it been operated for 8,760 hours during a calendar year at the base load rating. Actual and potential heat input derived from non-combustion sources (e.g., solar thermal) are not included when calculating the annual capacity factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Base load combustion turbine
rubrics_metrics.description: A stationary combustion turbine that supplies more than 40 percent of its potential electric output as net-electric sales on both a 12-operating month and a 3-year rolling average basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Base load rating
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum amount of heat input (fuel) that an EGU can combust on a steady state basis plus the maximum amount of heat input derived from non-combustion source (e.g., solar thermal), as determined by physical design and characteristics at ISO conditions. For a stationary combustion turbine, includes the heat input from duct burners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design efficiency and integrated equipment/energy storage output are included when determining base load rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Coal
rubrics_metrics.description: All solid fuels classified as anthracite, bituminous, subbituminous, or lignite in ASTM D388-99R04; coal refuse; petroleum coke; synthetic fuels derived from coal for creating useful heat (including solvent-refined coal, gasified coal not meeting natural gas definition, coal-oil mixtures, coal-water mixtures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Coal-fired Electric Generating Unit
rubrics_metrics.description: A steam generating unit or IGCC unit that combusts coal on or after the date of modification or at any point after December 31, 2029.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Combined cycle unit
rubrics_metrics.description: A stationary combustion turbine from which the heat from turbine exhaust gases is recovered by a heat recovery steam generating unit (HRSG) to generate additional electricity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Combined heat and power (CHP) unit
rubrics_metrics.description: An electric generating unit that simultaneously produces both electric (or mechanical) and useful thermal output from the same primary energy source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also known as 'cogeneration'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Design efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The rated overall net efficiency (e.g., electric plus useful thermal output) on a higher heating value basis at the base load rating, at ISO conditions, and at the maximum useful thermal output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design efficiency shall be determined using ASME PTC 22-2014, ASME PTC 46-1996, ISO 2314:2009 (E), or an alternative approved by the Administrator. When determining design efficiency, output of integrated equipment and energy storage is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Distillate oil
rubrics_metrics.description: Fuel oils complying with specifications for fuel oil numbers 1 and 2 (ASTM D396-98), diesel fuel oil numbers 1 and 2 (ASTM D975-08a), kerosene (ASTM D3699-08), biodiesel (ASTM D6751-11b), or biodiesel blends (ASTM D7467-10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References are incorporated by reference per §60.17.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Electric Generating Unit (EGU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any steam generating unit, IGCC unit, or stationary combustion turbine that is subject to this rule (i.e., meets the applicability criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Fossil fuel
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural gas, petroleum, coal, and any form of solid, liquid, or gaseous fuel derived from such material for creating useful heat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Gaseous fuel
rubrics_metrics.description: Any fuel present as a gas at ISO conditions, including natural gas, refinery/process gas, coke-oven gas, synthetic gas, gasified coal, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Gross energy output
rubrics_metrics.description: For stationary combustion turbines and IGCC: gross electric or direct mechanical output from the EGU plus 100% of useful thermal output. For steam generating units: gross electric/mechanical output from affected EGUs minus electricity used to power feedwater pumps plus 100% of useful thermal output. For CHP facilities meeting useful thermal output threshold, gross electric/mechanical output minus electricity for feedwater pumps, that difference divided by 0.95, plus 100% of useful thermal output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Heat recovery steam generating unit (HRSG)
rubrics_metrics.description: An EGU in which hot exhaust gases from the combustion turbine engine are routed to extract heat and generate useful output; can be used with or without duct burners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Integrated gasification combined cycle facility (IGCC)
rubrics_metrics.description: A combined cycle facility designed to burn fuels containing 50% or more solid-derived fuel (by heat input) not meeting natural gas definition, plus any integrated equipment providing electricity or useful thermal output to the affected EGU or auxiliary equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator may waive the 50% solid-derived fuel requirement during gasification system construction, startup/commissioning, shutdown, or repair. No solid fuel is directly burned in the EGU during operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Intermediate load combustion turbine
rubrics_metrics.description: A stationary combustion turbine that supplies more than 20 percent but less than or equal to 40 percent of its potential electric output as net-electric sales on both a 12-operating month and a 3-year rolling average basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: ISO conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: 288 Kelvin (15 °C, 59 °F), 60 percent relative humidity and 101.3 kilopascals (14.69 psi, 1 atm) pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Liquid fuel
rubrics_metrics.description: Any fuel present as a liquid at ISO conditions, including distillate oil and residual oil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Low load combustion turbine
rubrics_metrics.description: A stationary combustion turbine that supplies 20 percent or less of its potential electric output as net-electric sales on both a 12-operating month and a 3-year rolling average basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Mechanical output
rubrics_metrics.description: Useful mechanical energy not used to operate the affected EGU(s), generate electricity/thermal energy, or enhance performance of the affected EGU. Mechanical energy measured in horsepower hour should be converted into MWh by multiplying by 745.7 then dividing by 1,000,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Natural gas
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluid mixture of hydrocarbons (e.g., methane, ethane, or propane), composed of at least 70% methane by volume or gross calorific value between 35 and 41 MJ per dry standard cubic meter, that is gaseous at ISO conditions. Excludes landfill gas, digester gas, refinery gas, sour gas, blast furnace gas, coal-derived gas, producer gas, coke oven gas, or any gaseous fuel produced in a process that might result in highly variable CO2 content or heating value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Net-electric output
rubrics_metrics.description: Gross generation produced as measured at the generator terminals, less electricity used to operate the plant (auxiliary loads including fuel handling equipment, pumps, fans, pollution control equipment, other electricity needs, and transformer losses as measured at the transmission side of the step-up transformer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Net-electric sales
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Gross electric sales to the utility power distribution system minus purchased power; or (2) for CHP facilities meeting thermal output threshold, gross electric sales minus applicable percentage of purchased power of the thermal host(s). Includes electricity supplied to other facilities that produce electricity to offset auxiliary loads. Excludes electric sales during a system emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable percentage of purchased power for CHP facilities is determined based on percentage of total thermal load of the host facility supplied by the CHP facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Net energy output
rubrics_metrics.description: Net electric or mechanical output from the affected EGU plus 100% of useful thermal output; or for qualifying CHP facilities, net electric or mechanical output divided by 0.95 plus 100% of useful thermal output when thermal output meets threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Operating month
rubrics_metrics.description: A calendar month during which any fuel is combusted in the affected EGU at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Petroleum
rubrics_metrics.description: Crude oil or a fuel derived from crude oil, including distillate and residual oil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Potential electric output
rubrics_metrics.description: Base load rating design efficiency at maximum electric production rate multiplied by the base load rating (expressed in MMBtu/h), multiplied and converted per formula given to produce annual MWh potential (example calculation provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a 35% efficient EGU with 100 MW (341 MMBtu/h) fossil fuel heat input capacity would have a 306,000 MWh 12-month potential electric output capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Solid fuel
rubrics_metrics.description: Any fuel with definite shape and volume, not liquid or gaseous at ISO conditions; includes coal, biomass, and pulverized solid fuels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Standard ambient temperature and pressure (SATP) conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: 298.15 Kelvin (25 °C, 77 °F) and 100.0 kilopascals (14.504 psi, 0.987 atm) pressure. Enthalpy of water at SATP is 50 Btu/lb.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Stationary combustion turbine
rubrics_metrics.description: All equipment including turbine engine, fuel/air/lubrication/exhaust gas systems, control systems (except emissions control equipment), heat recovery system, fuel compressor, heater, pump, post-combustion emission control technology, and ancillary components comprising simple cycle, combined cycle, and CHP combustion turbine-based systems plus integrated equipment providing electricity or useful thermal output and integrated energy storage. 'Stationary' means not self-propelled or intended to be propelled while performing function; may be mounted on a vehicle for portability. A stationary combustion turbine that burns any solid fuel directly is considered a steam generating unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Steam generating unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Any furnace, boiler, or other device used for combusting fuel and producing steam (nuclear steam generators are not included) plus any integrated equipment that provides electricity or useful thermal output to the affected EGU(s) or auxiliary equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: System emergency
rubrics_metrics.description: Periods when the Reliability Coordinator has declared an Energy Emergency Alert level 2 or 3 as defined by NERC Reliability Standard EOP-011-2 or its successor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Useful thermal output
rubrics_metrics.description: Thermal energy made available for use in any heating application (e.g., steam delivered to an industrial process) that is not used for electric generation, mechanical output, to directly enhance EGU performance, or to supply energy to a pollution control device. Useful thermal output for EGUs with no condensate return is measured against SATP conditions; where condensate return has meaningful energy, energy in the condensate must be measured and subtracted relative to SATP from measured thermal output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economizer output is not useful thermal output; thermal energy used to reduce fuel moisture is considered useful thermal output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Valid data
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality-assured data generated by continuous monitoring systems installed, operated, and maintained according to part 75. For CEMS, initial certification requirements in 40 CFR 75.20 and appendix A to 40 CFR part 75 must be met before reporting quality-assured data; ongoing QA includes daily, quarterly, semiannual/annual test requirements and data validation criteria in appendix B to part 75. For fuel flow meters, initial certification per appendix D to part 75 (section 2.1.5) and ongoing QA per section 2.1.6 (with exceptions for qualifying commercial billing meters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the applicable sections of part 75 for certification and ongoing QA/validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Violation
rubrics_metrics.description: A specified averaging period over which the CO2 emissions rate is higher than the applicable emissions standard located in table 1 to this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan recordkeeping/monitoring/reporting requirement pointers (§60.5860b–60.5870b referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must address applicable monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements for affected EGUs and include recordkeeping, reporting, and notification requirements as provided in subsequent sections (§60.5865b–60.5870b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans must also address EGUs that commit to permanently cease operations by Jan 1, 2032 per §60.5876b and include procedures for submitting required information to EPA (§60.5875b).
